faqs.q: Sec. 54-155. - Parking violations involving signage, generally.
faqs.a:
(a)
Timed parking limitations.
When a traffic control sign is placed or posted giving notice that no vehicle may
               remain parked for longer than the time specified on the sign, it shall be unlawful
               for any person to park a vehicle longer than the maximum time specified on the sign.
(b)
Stopping or standing restrictions.
When a traffic control sign is placed or posted giving notice that no vehicle may
               be stopped or allowed to stand except in accordance with the limitation on the sign,
               including but not limited to a "loading" or "unloading" or "passenger pick up" or
               "drop off" sign, it shall be unlawful for any person to park, stand, or stop a vehicle
               in any manner in violation of that restriction.
(c)
Parking prohibitions.
When a traffic control sign is placed or posted giving notice of any parking, standing,
               or stopping prohibition, including but not limited to a "no parking," "no overnight
               parking," "no parking from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.," or "tow-away zone" sign, it shall
               be unlawful for any person to park, stop, or stand a vehicle in any manner in violation
               of that prohibition.
(i)
Moving parked vehicle in time limited parking zone.
Vehicles parked in a time limited zone shall be moved no less than 500 feet following
               the expiration of the posted parking time limit. Vehicle movement of less than 500
               feet or a vehicle being reparked within 500 feet of its recent location within a four-hour
               period of time will be considered to be remaining parked and is subject to a citation.
(d)
Exceptions.
(i)
Parking, standing, or stopping a vehicle in violation of a parking limitation, restriction,
               or prohibition sign is allowed when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic,
               or in compliance with the direction of a police officer.
(ii)
Food trucks or carts displaying a valid parking permit issued by the city are allowed
               to park, stand, or stop a vehicle in violation of a parking limitation, restriction,
               or prohibition sign so long as the parking, standing, or stopping activity is also
               in conformance with the conditions listed on the city permit.
(
Ord. No. 4561, § 2, 8-29-2016
)
